title: Classic Compass - Myth Maps & Modern Mashups
description: Join us for a teen lead workshop. Teens are invited to explore Greek and Roman myths and reimagine them through collage maps and creative writing prompts that connect ancient stories to modern ideas and media. Drop in anytime from 4-5pm. Available while supplies last. For teens ages 13-18.

title: Teen Mythology Guild
description: This session we are going to play some mythology themed trivia games.

title: Teen Mythology Guild: Norse Mythology Escape Room
Teen Mythology Guild: Gods & Goddesses of Earth, Harvest & Spring
Teen Mythology Guild: Dragons
description: In this session we are going to focus on dragons! Learn how these legendary creatures appear in myths from different countries. Get creative and craft your very own clay dragon eye and a dragon-themed bag charm. As a special bonus, every teen will receive a free book about dragons to keep the adventure going even after the program ends!

title: Teen Mythology Guild: Maya Folklore
description: In this session discover the rich mythology and artistry of the Maya. We will explore captivating stories such as the Hero Twins, Chechén and Chacá, and The Gift to the Hummingbird. Participants will also learn about the significance of the jade mosaic mask in Maya culture and create their own mini mosaic inspired by this ancient art form.

title: Teen Mythology Guild: Gods & Goddesses of the Sun
description: Step into the light and explore how ancient cultures understood the power of the sun. From the Egyptian sun god Ra to the Norse goddess Sunna, this program uncovers the myths, stories, and symbolism behind solar deities around the world. Make a sunburst with string art to take home.

title: Teen Mythology Guild: Indigenous Folklore
description: Learn about the origins of dreamcatchers in the traditions of the Ojibwe people and explore the deeper meanings behind this well-known symbol. We will look at Indigenous stories that highlight connections to nature, animals, and community. Teens will create a dreamcatcher-inspired craft while reflecting on themes of protection, dreams, and storytelling.

title: Teen Mythology Guild: Gods & Goddesses of Death
description: We will take a look at gods and goddesses from multiple cultures that represent death. From the Greek god Hades to the Aztec goddess Coatlicue, we will take a closer look on how gods/goddess of death are depicted in stories. We will make a split mask inspired by the Norse goddess Hel.

title: Teen Mythology Guild: Korean Folklore
description: Explore the stories of the Heavenly Maiden and the Woodcutter and The Legend of the Green Frog. Make a tiny frog faux terrarium to take home. Learn about the folk art and rituals that inspired K-Pop Demon Hunters.

title: Teen Mythology Guild: Gods & Goddesses of Fate
description: Learn about the Greek sisters who control the thread of human life, the Baltic goddess Laima, the Hattian goddesses Istustaya and Papaya and more.

title: Mythology Guild for Tweens
description: June will focus on Greek mythology! Join us to learn about what the Ancient Greeks believed and some of the things they did to honor their gods and goddesses. We will do some cool crafts and a snack will be provided.

title: Mythology Guild for Tweens
description: July will focus on Ancient Egyptian mythology! Join us to learn about what the Ancient Egyptians believed and some of the things they did to honor their gods and goddesses. We will do some cool crafts and a snack will be provided.

title: Stories That Shape Us
description: Each participant will receive a research kit including a journal, sketch book, art supplies, bookmark, poem magnets and more!

title: Stories That Shape Us Showcase
description: Teens in our youth-led humanities group have been exploring folklore from a wide range of cultures. Each week, they’ve delved into legends, ancient tales, family traditions, and myths, discovering the stories that shape different communities. The artwork and creative writing on display reflect their interpretations of these meaningful stories.

title: Wonder Time: Mythology with a Classic Compass
description: First Wonder Time of the Summer ☀ Mythology, mazes & more!

title: From Erie to Seoul: NSLI-Y & International Exchange
description:
This workshop will introduce high school students to National Security Language Initiative for Youth (NSLI-Y) and international exchange opportunities.

Join us as NSLI-Y alumna Silvia Kang shares her experience studying Korean in Seoul through NSLI-Y. Fulbright FLTAs Yu Jen Chang and Rania Al Qiq from Mercyhurst University will also join us to discuss their cultures, Fulbright experiences, language learning, and international exchange.

The program will conclude with a Q&A and resources for students interested in these opportunities.

This program is presented in partnership with Classic Compass. For teens ages 13-18. This program is free. No registration is required.

title: Discover Korean: Language, Stories, and Culture
description:
This interactive workshop will introduce students to Hangul, Korean greetings and useful phrases, and Korean language and culture. Participants will have the opportunity to learn how to write their names in Korean, try tasty Korean snacks, and play some fun games.

The workshop will feature National Security Language Initiative for Youth (NSLI-Y) Alumni Voices — selected short videos and written reflections from four NSLI-Y alumni, offering different perspectives on language immersion, cultural exchange, and their experiences studying abroad through NSLI-Y.

This program is presented in partnership with Classic Compass. For teens ages 13-18. This program is free. No registration is required.
